name: Fool's Day
summary: A dying bell-jingler hands us a rhyming letter: the Lord of Fools has taken Wickermoor, and every friend we have is dancing in his costumes.

stages.journal: A reveler in a coat of bells fell dead at our feet with a wax-sealed letter in rhyme. Under the costume was Bess Crumley, from the Green Queen. The letter says all our friends will be at a party.
stages.hint: Go back into Wickermoor, where the music is coming from.

stages.journal: The village has swollen to three times its size, and a crowd of costumed dancers is shoving us toward the middle of it.
stages.hint: Follow the crowd to the Festival Square, or fight your way out of it.

stages.journal: In the square a puppet jester fell out of the sky into a net and explained the rules: win tickets at the booths, spend them on our friends, or find them ourselves.
stages.hint: Find the costumed friends and free them: tickets, a fight, a spell, or a quiet church.

stages.journal: Twelve of our friends are forced revelers in the old troupe's costumes. Every one we free makes the next dearer at the Prize Counter.
stages.hint: Free the rest of the revelers, or tell Chuckles to his face how much you hate him.

stages.journal: The parade has begun. Two masked Heralds lead it, and anyone we have not freed is dancing in it.
stages.hint: Face the Heralds in the Festival Square.

stages.journal: The Heralds' masks cracked. Under them were Phillip and Adela Druskenvald, smiling through paint like blood. Chuckles turned them to streamers.
stages.hint: Go to the Ring of Fools.

stages.journal: In the Ring of Fools the jester was only a picture. The real Lord of Fools is the balloon on the pole.
Chuckles went up in a firework of his own grinning face. The town shrank back to its size and the rescued gathered to piece together what they had been.
